title: Over 50,000 Saplings Planted Across 31 States on Hariyali Amavasya Under Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative
subtitle:
Vriksh Mitra Parivar Drives Nationwide Plantation Campaign Under PM Modi’s ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ Call
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Leads Major Tree Plantation Drive in Delhi on Hariyali Amavasya
Vriksh Mitra Parivar Emerges as the Face of a Nationwide Green Movement
Planting Trees Means Securing the Future: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Respect for Nature Is the Best Way to Protect Future Generations; The Real Commitment Is to Save Trees, Not Just Plant Them: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Delhi Has Learnt Much from Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative, Says Minister Shri Manjinder Singh Sirsa
Development Must Go Hand in Hand with Environmental Protection, Says Minister Shri Parvesh Verma
body_text:
More than 50,000 saplings were planted across 31 states on the occasion of Hariyali Amavasya as part of a nationwide plantation drive led by Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan in collaboration with the “Vriksh Mitra Parivar.” The campaign drew further momentum from Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative. The program was held at the PBG Ground, Central Ridge, near Talkatora Stadium in New Delhi, where ministers, Members of Parliament, government officials, farmers, youth and citizens participated in the plantation drive. The program began with the watering of saplings and the singing of Vande Mataram, followed by mass plantation. Similar plantation drives were organised across villages, towns, panchayats and institutions in different parts of the country. Members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar played a key role in mobilising citizens and encouraging them to plant at least one tree.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan said Hariyali Amavasya is not only a religious occasion but also an opportunity to express gratitude towards nature. He said Indian traditions view human beings, animals, birds, rivers, mountains and trees as interconnected elements of the natural ecosystem. “Planting a tree is not just about adding greenery; it is an investment in the future of coming generations,” Shri Chouhan said, stressing that planting saplings must be accompanied by a commitment to their protection and regular care. The Union Minister urged every citizen to plant at least one tree each year and encourage five others to join the campaign. He suggested observing birthdays, wedding anniversaries, the birth of children and the death anniversaries of parents as “Vriksh Parv” by planting trees.
Shri Chouhan also called upon panchayats, urban local bodies and institutions to identify designated areas for plantation so that saplings can be protected and maintained over the long term. Highlighting the close link between environmental sustainability and agriculture, Shri Chouhan said environmental degradation directly affects farming, water availability, soil health and human well-being. He said that for farmers, access to water and maintaining soil health are as important as the availability of seeds and fertilisers. He called for greater adoption of Mission LiFE, energy conservation and reduced dependence on plastic to strengthen environmental protection. “Nature must not be exploited; its resources must be used responsibly and conserved for the future,” he said.
Delhi government's Cabinet Minister Shri Manjinder Singh Sirsa said the Delhi Government had drawn valuable lessons from Shri Chouhan’s initiative. He said more than one lakh people in Delhi have been connected with the campaign, while schools, colleges and other institutions are also being encouraged to participate in plantation activities. Shri Sirsa said citizens are increasingly coming forward to take a collective pledge for environmental protection and contribute to the plantation drive.
Delhi government's Cabinet Minister Shri Parvesh Verma said the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative should inspire every citizen to take responsibility for protecting the environment. He said development and environmental conservation must go hand in hand, adding that sustainable development requires a balance between infrastructure expansion and preservation of green cover.
The program was attended by Member of Parliament Shri Darshan Singh Choudhary, representatives of various institutions, officials from agricultural universities, personnel from ICAR, DARE and KVKs, and a large number of members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar. The nationwide drive was positioned as a tree plantation exercise as well as an effort to build sustained public participation in environmental conservation. The campaign emphasised that planting a sapling is only the first step, while ensuring its survival and growth is an equally important responsibility. Members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar are continuing to take this message to communities across the country.

enrichment.summary: On Hariyali Amavasya (12 August 2026), Union Agriculture & Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan led a nationwide tree plantation drive with the 'Vriksh Mitra Parivar', under which more than 50,000 saplings were planted across 31 states. The main event was held at PBG Ground, Central Ridge, near Talkatora Stadium, New Delhi, drawing momentum from PM Modi's 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiative. Chouhan urged citizens to plant at least one tree annually, protect existing plantations, and adopt Mission LiFE practices, while Delhi ministers Manjinder Singh Sirsa and Parvesh Verma highlighted complementary state-level efforts and the need to balance development with environmental protection.
enrichment.context: 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' (A Tree in the Name of Mother) is a nationwide afforestation campaign launched by the Government of India to encourage citizens to plant trees dedicated to their mothers, symbolically linking environmental stewardship with familial and cultural values; it complements India's broader climate commitments, including its NDC pledge to create additional carbon sinks of 2.5-3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through forest and tree cover by 2030 under the Paris Agreement. Hariyali Amavasya, a traditional occasion in parts of India (notably Madhya Pradesh) associated with tree worship and plantation, has increasingly been leveraged by the government to mobilise mass plantation drives, reflecting a trend of embedding environmental messaging within religious-cultural observances to widen public participation. Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), referenced by Chouhan, is a global initiative launched by India at COP26 promoting individual and community-level pro-environment behavioural change, and is a recurring theme in India's environmental governance discourse. Such plantation drives, though partly ceremonial, are part of larger governmental efforts—alongside programmes like the National Afforestation Programme, CAMPA, and state-level green missions—to increase forest and tree cover, address land degradation, and support agriculture-linked ecological concerns such as soil health and water availability, which the minister explicitly connected to farmers' welfare.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' plantation initiative, referenced in a recent nationwide tree plantation drive, was launched under the call of which of the following?
options: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change alone
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the plantation campaign drew momentum from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiative.

prelims_questions.question: 'Mission LiFE', mentioned in the context of India's environmental conservation efforts, primarily promotes which of the following?
options: Individual and community-level pro-environment lifestyle changes
Compulsory afforestation by private corporations only
Replacement of fossil fuel vehicles with electric vehicles
prelims_questions.explanation: Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) is a global initiative encouraging individual and collective behavioural change towards environmentally conscious living, as referenced by the minister in the release.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of mass afforestation campaigns like 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' in India's efforts to meet its climate commitments under the Paris Agreement. What challenges hinder the long-term survival of planted saplings, and how can governance mechanisms address them?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Environment and Climate Change

mains_questions.question: Examine the interlinkages between environmental degradation and agricultural productivity in India, particularly with reference to soil health and water availability. How can government policy better integrate environmental conservation with farmer welfare?
